correctness.summary: Let M=Ran p(T). It is T-invariant and has dimension r. Cayley-Hamilton on T|M yields an annihilating polynomial of degree at most d+r. A complemented block decomposition makes the quotient block p-algebraic and gives a correction F with Ran F contained in M and rank at most r. The noncommutative telescoping identity writes p(T)-p(S) as d terms factoring through T-S, proving rank p(T) <= d rank(T-S). Jordan, scalar, and cyclic-shift examples attain the stated bounds.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Barnes (1985), Corollary 11, gives existence of some finite-rank J with p(T-J)=0 when p(T) has finite-dimensional range, but does not state the defect-range localization, rank bound, sharp degree bound, or two-sided rank-distance estimate. Alvarez (2014) treats polynomially finite-rank linear relations via Fredholm/Riesz-Schauder theory. No exact quantitative statement was located in the inspected literature. Kramar (2012) is a residual risk because only its abstract, not full text, was inspected.

value.summary: The theorem gives sharp quantitative control from the single defect rank r: minimal-polynomial degree at most d+r, a correction supported inside the defect range with no rank inflation, and rank distance to the p-algebraic locus between ceil(r/d) and r with optimal universal constants.

limitations: Originality is only to the best of our knowledge.
The full text of Kramar (2012) was not inspected; only its abstract was available.
The lower factor 1/d is sharp as a universal degree-d constant, not necessarily for every fixed polynomial.
Very old or poorly indexed equivalent formulations may not have been located.
Independent audit has not been performed.
